subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
notes: Ethics and governance core. No numerical questions apply; extra objective and case items included.

questions.text: The moral principles that guide business conduct are
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Business ethics are the standards of right and wrong in business.

questions.text: The principles of honesty fairness and integrity form the core of
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Honesty fairness and integrity are fundamental ethical values.

questions.text: A written statement of an organisations ethical principles is a code of
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: A code of ethics guides employee conduct in an organisation.

questions.text: Ethics and law are identical because all legal actions are ethical
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Some actions are legal but unethical and some ethical actions may go beyond law.

questions.text: State the sources of business ethics
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Religion culture law society and personal values shape business ethics.
questions.explanation: Ethical standards emerge from these social and personal sources.

questions.text: Explain the importance of business ethics
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Business ethics builds trust and reputation attracts customers and talent reduces legal risk and supports long term sustainability and social legitimacy.
questions.explanation: Cover trust reputation and long term sustainability.

questions.text: The process of choosing between right and wrong alternatives is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Ethical decision making evaluates alternatives by moral standards.

questions.text: A situation with two conflicting but valid moral choices is an ethical
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: An ethical dilemma forces a choice between conflicting moral principles.

questions.text: Utilitarianism judges actions by their consequences for overall happiness
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Utilitarianism evaluates actions by their consequences for the greatest good.

questions.text: List the stages of ethical decision making
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Identifying the issue gathering facts evaluating alternatives deciding and reviewing the outcome.
questions.explanation: These steps structure an ethical decision.

questions.text: Explain the theories of business ethics
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: The main theories are utilitarianism deontology and virtue ethics which judge actions by consequences duties or the character of the agent respectively.
questions.explanation: Contrast consequentialist duty based and virtue approaches.

questions.text: Ethics applied to marketing advertising and pricing is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Marketing ethics governs honest advertising pricing and selling.

questions.text: Misleading or false advertising is an unethical marketing practice
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Deceptive advertising misleads consumers and violates ethics.

questions.text: Manipulating financial statements to mislead investors is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Window dressing presents a misleadingly favourable financial picture.

questions.text: List ethical issues in human resource management
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Discrimination favouritism unsafe conditions and unfair compensation.
questions.explanation: These issues raise ethical concerns in managing people.

questions.text: Explain the ethical issues in marketing
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Marketing ethics covers deceptive advertising unsafe products misleading pricing and manipulative selling all of which harm consumers and breach trust.
questions.explanation: Describe each marketing ethics issue and its harm.

questions.text: The system by which companies are directed and controlled is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Corporate governance is the framework for directing and controlling companies.

questions.text: The body elected by shareholders to oversee management is the board of
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: The board of directors represents shareholders and oversees management.

questions.text: Transparency accountability fairness and responsibility are principles of good governance
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: These four pillars underpin sound corporate governance.

questions.text: List the pillars of corporate governance
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: These pillars guide how companies should be governed.

questions.text: Explain the role of the board of directors in governance
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: The board sets strategy oversees management ensures accountability protects shareholder interests and monitors risk and compliance.
questions.explanation: Cover strategy oversight accountability and risk monitoring.

questions.text: The commitment of business to contribute to sustainable development is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: CSR is a firms commitment to society beyond its legal and economic duties.

questions.text: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Sustainable development balances present needs and future resources.

questions.text: In India CSR spending is mandatory for large companies above specified thresholds
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: The Companies Act mandates CSR spending for qualifying companies.

questions.text: List the arguments for corporate social responsibility
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Improved reputation customer loyalty employee morale and long term profitability.
questions.explanation: CSR builds goodwill that supports business success.

questions.text: Explain the benefits of corporate social responsibility
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: CSR enhances reputation attracts customers and talent reduces regulatory risk and creates long term value by aligning business with societal interests.
questions.explanation: Cover reputation talent and long term value benefits.

questions.text: Reporting misconduct within an organisation is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Whistleblowing is disclosing wrongdoing within an organisation.

questions.text: The shared values and norms that guide ethical behaviour form the
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Ethical culture is the environment of shared ethical values and practices.

questions.text: Whistleblowers should be protected from retaliation
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Protection encourages reporting of wrongdoing without fear of reprisal.

questions.text: List the ways to build an ethical culture in an organisation
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership example codes of ethics training open communication and fair enforcement.
questions.explanation: These practices embed ethics in organisational life.

questions.text: Explain the importance of whistleblowing in organisations
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Whistleblowing exposes fraud and misconduct early protecting stakeholders and the public and reinforcing accountability and ethical standards.
questions.explanation: Cover early detection and accountability benefits.

questions.text: Assertion: Ethical leadership promotes an ethical culture. Reason: Employees model their behaviour on the example set by leaders
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: Leaders set the ethical tone that employees follow.

questions.text: Match the concept to its meaning
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Ethics are moral principles while law is binding and CSR is societal commitment.

questions.text: The philosophy that the only obligation of business is to increase profits is the
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Shareholder theory holds that profit maximisation is the sole business duty.

questions.text: The theory that business should serve all parties affected by it is
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Stakeholder theory says firms should balance the interests of all stakeholders.

questions.text: Explain the relationship between ethics and corporate governance
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Ethics provides the values that governance structures enforce so good governance institutionalises ethical behaviour through boards codes and accountability.
questions.explanation: Link ethical values to governance mechanisms.

questions.text: Read the case: A sales manager is tempted to overstate product benefits to meet targets. Explain the ethical dilemma and the right course
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: The dilemma is between meeting targets and honest marketing. The right course is to be truthful about benefits because misleading customers is unethical and harms trust.
questions.explanation: Apply ethical reasoning to the conflict between targets and honesty.

questions.text: Read the case: An employee discovers fraudulent accounting but fears losing his job if he reports it. Explain his options and the protection available
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: The employee should report through the whistleblower channel and is protected by whistleblower policies and law against retaliation.
questions.explanation: Apply whistleblowing and the protections that encourage reporting.

questions.text: Explain the factors that influence ethical behaviour in organisations
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Ethical behaviour is shaped by individual values the ethical climate leadership example codes and reward systems of the organisation.
questions.explanation: Cover individual and organisational determinants of ethics.

questions.text: List the benefits of good corporate governance
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Investor confidence better access to capital reduced risk and long term value.
questions.explanation: Good governance attracts investment and reduces risk.

questions.text: Explain the corporate governance framework in India
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Indian governance is set by the Companies Act SEBI regulations and clause 49 covering board composition audit committees and disclosure requirements.
questions.explanation: Cover the legal and regulatory framework of governance.

questions.text: The conflict of interest between shareholders and managers is the agency
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: The agency problem is the conflict between owners and managers.

questions.text: Explain the arguments against corporate social responsibility
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Critics argue CSR raises costs dilutes the profit focus and imposes social duties on business that belong to government.
questions.explanation: Present the cost and role dilution arguments against CSR.

questions.text: A company that is ethical in all dealings with stakeholders follows an ethics based approach
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: An ethics based approach applies moral standards to all stakeholder dealings.

questions.text: Explain the ethical issues in finance and accounting
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Finance ethics covers insider trading fraud window dressing and misrepresentation of accounts all of which mislead investors and breach trust.
questions.explanation: Describe each financial ethics issue and its impact.

questions.text: Trading shares using confidential information is insider trading
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.explanation: Insider trading is using non public information for personal gain.

questions.text: Explain the role of leadership in promoting business ethics
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders model ethical behaviour set the tone communicate values and reward integrity thereby embedding ethics in the organisation culture.
questions.explanation: Cover modelling tone setting and reinforcement.

questions.text: List the elements of an effective code of ethics
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Clear values specific guidance examples reporting procedures and enforcement.
questions.explanation: These elements make a code practical and enforceable.

questions.text: Explain the concept of sustainable development
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising future generations by balancing economic environmental and social goals.
questions.explanation: Cover the three pillars of sustainability.

questions.text: Explain the steps an organisation can take to institutionalise ethics
questions.subject: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
questions.correctAnswer: Institutionalising ethics requires leadership commitment a code of ethics training communication and enforcement through reward and sanction.
questions.explanation: Cover the mechanisms that embed ethics organisationally.
